report_name: CISA and FBI Warn of Attacks on US Water System PLCs

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Malicious actors gained initial access to water systems by exploiting internet-exposed Rockwell Automation MicroLogix PLCs.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors likely gained access to PLCs by using default or weak credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: The presence of undocumented cellular modems suggests attackers exploited remote services to gain initial access to the OT network.

attack_patterns.name: Service Stop
attack_patterns.description: Attackers altered PLC configurations, including changing IP addresses, which stopped the service and severed the connection to SCADA systems, causing a denial of service.

attack_patterns.name: Manipulation of Control
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors manipulated control of PLCs by changing device passwords and altering IP addresses, locking out legitimate operators and disrupting physical processes like water pressure.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Adversaries scanned the internet for exposed OT devices, such as Rockwell PLCs, likely using tools like Shodan to identify vulnerable targets.

tools.name: Shodan
tools.description: A search engine likely used by attackers for reconnaissance to identify vulnerable, internet-accessible PLCs.

tools.name: RSLogix
tools.description: Rockwell Automation programming software whose unexpected usage from unauthorized workstations is a potential indicator of malicious activity to modify PLC logic.

campaigns.name: Campaign against US Water Systems
campaigns.description: A coordinated campaign in July 2026 where malicious actors targeted internet-exposed Rockwell Automation PLCs in the U.S. Water and Wastewater Systems (WWS) sector, leading to significant operational disruptions.
campaigns.objective: Disrupt operations of US water and wastewater facilities.

identities.name: U.S. Water and Wastewater Systems (WWS) Sector
identities.description: A critical infrastructure sector in the United States targeted by cyberattacks against internet-exposed Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), resulting in operational disruptions like flooding and loss of water pressure.

identities.name: Rockwell Automation
identities.description: Vendor of the Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 series PLCs that were targeted in the attacks. The company provided guidance for recovering locked controllers.

indicators.name: Anomalous Inbound Traffic to EtherNet/IP Ports
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Inbound Traffic to EtherNet/IP Ports
id: 2b8c1f3a-5d6e-4b9f-8c1d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects unexpected inbound network traffic to default EtherNet/IP ports (44818/TCP, 2222/TCP) used by Rockwell PLCs. Such traffic from external sources could indicate reconnaissance or an attempt to exploit exposed OT devices.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/07/30/cisa-urges-water-and-wastewater-systems-sector-protect-ot-against-activity-targeting-plcs
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-31
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1595
level: high
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    dst_port:
      - 44818
      - 2222
    protocol: 'tcp'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects inbound network traffic to default Rockwell PLC ports (44818/TCP, 2222/TCP), which is highly suspicious if originating from the internet and targeting an OT network.

indicators.name: Unexpected RSLogix Software Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Unexpected RSLogix Software Execution
id: f9e8d7c6-b5a4-4321-b098-7a6b5c4d3e2f
status: experimental
description: Monitors for the execution of Rockwell RSLogix programming software, which could indicate unauthorized attempts to modify PLC logic or configurations.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/07/30/cisa-urges-water-and-wastewater-systems-sector-protect-ot-against-activity-targeting-plcs
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-31
tags:
  - attack.t0831
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\RSLogix500.exe'
      - '\RSLogix5000.exe'
      - '\Studio5000.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of Rockwell RSLogix programming software, which could indicate an unauthorized user attempting to connect to and modify PLC configurations.

relationships.target_name: U.S. Water and Wastewater Systems (WWS) Sector

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Inbound Traffic to EtherNet/IP Ports
